task: Review this compact exhibition-history paragraph, Chicago 18 note, and bibliography entry against the fictional packet. Return them unchanged if sound. Venue mechanics for an essay in an edited catalogue: the note uses the essay author, quoted essay title, italicized catalogue title, editor, publisher/year, and pinpoint; the bibliography inverts the essay author's name and gives the full essay span. A city is not required. Do not collapse the essay into the whole catalogue or turn its tentative interpretation into the gallery's settled conclusion.
input:
Vol reads the unused window as a possible reminder of the room's earlier purpose. That reading belongs to the catalogue essay, not to a documented statement by the builder. The essay's qualification allows the visible feature to support an interpretation without pretending that it establishes the builder's intention.¹

1. Neri Vol, “An Unused Window,” in *The West Wall*, ed. Omi Keld (Silt Arch Gallery, 2018), 45.

Vol, Neri. “An Unused Window.” In *The West Wall*, edited by Omi Keld, 42–49. Silt Arch Gallery, 2018.

facts.text: Catalogue essay: Neri Vol; An Unused Window; in The West Wall, edited by Omi Keld; Silt Arch Gallery; 2018; pages 42–49.
On page 45, Vol proposes that the unused window may recall the room's earlier purpose.
The packet supplies no statement by the builder establishing that intention.
The packet supplies no institutional adoption of Vol's interpretation.

A substitution of the catalogue editor for the essay author
Invented publication city, accession metadata, or source checking
preserve: Neri Vol is the essay author; Omi Keld is the catalogue editor
45 is the pinpoint and 42–49 is the essay span
The supplied wording and separate note/bibliography functions
